title: Pool Leak Detection & Repair
metaTitle: Pool Leak Repair in Riverside County | Rivera Pools
metaDescription: Pool leak repair and water-loss assessment in Riverside County. Investigate evaporation, plumbing, shell, equipment, skimmer, and return leaks.
intro: Pool leak repair in Riverside County starts with a focused water-loss assessment so a hidden plumbing, shell, equipment, or fitting problem is not mistaken for evaporation.
problem: A falling water level can come from evaporation, a shell, plumbing, skimmer, return, equipment, or a leak that appears only when the system runs. Repeatedly adding water does not identify the source.
solution: We document the pattern, inspect visible conditions, and use appropriate testing to narrow the likely source. The findings can guide a focused repair or be coordinated with resurfacing and remodeling.
materials: Shell, skimmer, return, and equipment checks
Visual, dye, or pressure testing when appropriate
Repair planning with resurfacing or tile work

faqs.q: How can I tell if my pool is leaking or evaporating?
faqs.a: A controlled water-loss comparison can help separate evaporation from a leak. Equipment operation, weather, plumbing, shell condition, and wet areas also matter, so an assessment is more reliable than guessing.

faqs.q: Can you find a leak under the deck?
faqs.a: We can inspect visible conditions and use appropriate testing to narrow the likely source. Access, plumbing layout, and the type of leak determine what can be confirmed and repaired.

faqs.q: Should leak detection happen before resurfacing?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Finding and planning around water loss before a new finish is installed helps prevent the renovation from hiding an unresolved problem.

faqs.q: When should I call for pool leak repair in Riverside County?
faqs.a: Call when the water level drops repeatedly, the pump loses prime, air enters the system, wet soil appears near the pool, or you are adding water often enough that evaporation no longer explains the loss.
